name: Cotton
model: written by hand (Claude) from the Urdu KB

aspects.overview:
Cotton, 'white gold', is Pakistan's key cash crop: its fibre feeds the textile industry and earns foreign exchange, and cottonseed oil is used for vanaspati ghee. Punjab produces about 70 percent of Pakistan's cotton. Punjab yields: about 16.3 maunds per acre in 2019-20, 15.8 in 2020-21, 19.6 in 2021-22, 10.5 in 2022-23 (rain and heat damage), 17.4 in 2023-24 and 14.3 in 2024-25, on 3.2 to 4.6 million acres.
Best soil: fertile loam that becomes crumbly after preparation, rich in organic matter, holds moisture long, with no hard layer below. Early sowing (February–March) suits the districts of Multan, Sahiwal, Faisalabad, Sargodha and Dera Ghazi Khan divisions; it has its own production technology because the weather then is different.
Heat stress damages leaf cells, breathing and food making, so flowers, squares and small bolls drop and the remaining bolls give poor-quality cotton; care during heat waves matters.
Bt varieties protect against bollworms (caterpillars); non-Bt varieties don't, and get more pest attack.
Better Cotton principles: reduce harmful crop-protection effects, use water efficiently, care for soil health, protect natural habitats, protect fibre quality, and manage the crop well with climate change in mind.
aspects.fertilizer:
Base fertilizer on a soil test (Agriculture Department labs in every Punjab district), variety, sowing method and time, and previous crop. The free 'Khaad Hisab' app from the Soil Fertility Institute Punjab calculates amounts.
Early-sown cotton, per acre:
Weak soil (115 kg N, 45 kg P, 38 kg K): 2 bags DAP + 4.25 bags urea + 1.5 bags SOP (or 1.25 bags MOP); or 5 bags SSP + 5 bags urea + 1.5 SOP; or 4.5 bags Nitrophos + 2.75 bags urea + 1.5 SOP; or 4.5 bags Nitrophos + 5 bags CAN + 1.5 SOP.
Medium soil (100 N, 40 P, 38 K): 1.75 DAP + 3.75 urea + 1.5 SOP; or 4.5 SSP + 4.25 urea + 1.5 SOP; or 4 Nitrophos + 2.5 urea + 1.5 SOP; or 4 Nitrophos + 4.25 CAN + 1.5 SOP.
Fertile soil (90 N, 35 P, 38 K): 1.5 DAP + 3.25 urea + 1.5 SOP; or 4 SSP + 4 urea + 1.5 SOP; or 3.5 Nitrophos + 2.25 urea + 1.5 SOP; or 3.5 Nitrophos + 4 CAN + 1.5 SOP.
Bt cotton, central (main) areas:
Weak soil (100 N, 40 P, 38 K): 1.75 DAP + 3.5 urea + 1.5 SOP (or 1.25 MOP); or 4.5 SSP + 4.25 urea + 1.5 SOP; or 4 Nitrophos + 2.5 urea + 1.5 SOP.
Medium soil (90 N, 35 P, 38 K): 1.5 DAP + 3.25 urea + 1.5 SOP; or 4 SSP + 4 urea + 1.5 SOP; or 3.5 Nitrophos + 2.25 urea + 1.5 SOP.
Fertile soil (80 N, 30 P, 38 K): 1.25 DAP + 3 urea + 1.5 SOP; or 3.5 SSP + 3.5 urea + 1.5 SOP; or 3 Nitrophos + 2 urea + 1.5 SOP.
Bt cotton, secondary areas: weak soil 90 N, 40 P, 30 K (about 1.75 DAP + 3.25 urea + 1.25 SOP); medium 80 N, 35 P, 30 K (about 1.5 DAP + 3 urea + 1.25 SOP); fertile 70 N, 30 P, 30 K (about 1.25 DAP + 2.5 urea + 1.25 SOP).
Non-Bt cotton: central areas 69 N, 35 P, 25 K; secondary areas 58 N, 35 P, 25 K per acre.
Timing: put all phosphorus and potash and one quarter of the nitrogen at land preparation, close to the seed (fertilizer near the seed works about twice as well). If missed, give it after thinning: put phosphorus in the furrows and hoe, or dissolve Nitrophos in irrigation water. Give the rest of the nitrogen in 3 to 5 splits at flowering, boll formation and after the first picking; finish by the last week of August. Always add nitrogen after heavy rain. On dry soil irrigate right after nitrogen and apply in the evening. On sandy soil split potash: at sowing and at boll formation. For better results spray potassium nitrate 2 percent weekly, four times, from flowering.
Zinc and boron: zinc sulphate 33% 5 kg (or 21% 6 to 10 kg) and boric acid 17% 2.5 kg (or borax 11% 3.5 kg) per acre. Or spray three times at 45, 60 and 90 days after sowing: 300 g boric acid 17%, 250 g zinc sulphate 33% and 50 g washing powder in 100 litres of water. Don't mix with insecticides; spray upper leaves in the morning or evening, never at midday (leaf burn).
After rain, spray 500 g magnesium sulphate + 2 kg urea per acre to help plants recover.
Deficiency signs: nitrogen – old lower leaves turn light green then yellow, growth stops; phosphorus – short plants, dark green leaves, late bolls, yellow lower stem; potash – leaf edges yellow then scorched, red midribs; zinc – small yellow young leaves, short internodes, rusty look; boron – yellowing, wrinkled leaves curling down.
Nutrients per 50 kg bag: urea 23 kg N; CAN 13 kg N; TSP 23 kg P; SSP 9 kg P; DAP 9 kg N + 23 kg P; Nitrophos 11 kg N + 10 kg P; SOP 25 kg K; MOP 30 kg K.
Soil health: add organic matter (green manure, farmyard manure), rotate with legumes, never burn residues (mix them in with a rotavator or disc, or compost them), use integrated nutrients and mulching.
aspects.irrigation:
Bed (ridge) sown cotton: after the sowing irrigation give the first water 3 to 4 days later (by weather and soil), the 2nd, 3rd and 4th at 6 to 9 day intervals, then as the crop needs. Drill-sown cotton: after the first irrigation, water every 12 to 15 days. If wheat follows cotton, give the last irrigation by 10 October (drill) or 15 October (beds).
Water scouting: at about 8 am walk a few steps into the field from a corner and check 6 plants for: 1) wilted top leaves, 2) red colour on the upper three-quarters of the stem, 3) the tip bending instead of snapping with a crack when broken, 4) soil from 2 inches deep under the canopy not forming a ball when squeezed, 5) shorter internodes, 6) white flowers at the top of the plant. Check three places; if 4 of the 6 signs show, irrigate. Signs appear first on high and saline patches. Irrigate before stress shows.
In heat waves water in the evening or at night, not in the hot day (it drives oxygen out of the soil), and give light irrigations often instead of one heavy one. Water shortage at flowering, squaring and small-boll stage makes them drop and lowers quality.
aspects.harvesting:
Picking: start when 40 to 50 percent of bolls are open. Pick after the dew dries and stop at 4 pm. Don't pick when rain is expected; after rain wait until the cotton is fully dry. Pick from the bottom of the plant upward so dry leaves don't mix in, and pick only fully open bolls. Pick American cotton every 15 to 20 days and desi cotton every 8 days. Finish before severe cold. Pay pickers well and by cleanliness so they don't add green bolls; have them work in one row in one direction under a supervisor, use cotton cloth (jholi), cover their heads, and carry cotton in cotton-cloth bags (not jute, polythene or plastic), stitched without jute or plastic string. Keep fallen and trash-mixed cotton, the last picking (weak fibre, seed not fit to sow), pink-bollworm-damaged bolls and different varieties separate.
Storage: keep moisture of seed cotton (phutti) at 8 to 10 percent or less, in an airy store with a dry pucca floor (on a kacha floor lay plastic, dry sand, then plastic). Stack in heaps with gaps for air. Outside, keep it on high dry ground on sand and plastic, cover in rain, and sell quickly. Store seed sun-dried in jute or cloth bags in a dry airy store, raised off the floor, never in nylon or plastic bags.
After picking: let sheep and goats graze leftover bolls, or remove them with a pink bollworm manager (bonja) machine. Fumigate seed cotton kept for seed with 30 aluminium phosphide tablets per 1,000 cubic feet against pink bollworm. Cut sticks at ground level; bury them with a rotavator or remove them and plough deep. Keep fuel sticks far from cotton fields, standing upright in small heaps no higher than 5 feet, and turn them in February–March to kill pink bollworm pupae. Irrigate the field in winter to kill hibernating pink bollworm. Clean ginning factory waste. Picking runs from September to October.
aspects.machinery: If a hard layer has formed, plough deep with a chisel plough, preferably twice crosswise, so roots go deep and moisture lasts. Sow with a kharif drill or a bed-making planter where available; the field must be level and the machine set to the recommended plant population. Use a rotavator or disc to mix residues and bury sticks after the last picking.
aspects.other: Climate change (untimely rain, unusual heat) has hurt cotton yields and pest pressure and changed sowing time. Cotton now matures earlier (many varieties by November), making it easier to sow wheat, winter vegetables and pulses after it. Protect biodiversity: don't clear forests, bird habitats, natural pastures or lakes for cotton, and grow a few plants whose seeds attract birds, which also eat pests.
aspects.pests_diseases:
Approach: integrated pest management. Scout weekly (twice in emergencies), in the morning or evening; on big farms scout 5 acres of every 25, each variety separately. For sucking pests check leaves (top, middle, bottom) of 20 plants; for bollworms check 25 plants (5 at 5 spots). Avoid insecticide sprays in the first 60 days unless attack is heavy and the local Agriculture Extension / Pest Warning staff advise it. Spray only at the economic threshold, rotate products, use registered products with Urdu labels (never those banned under the Stockholm Convention), spray with a power or hand sprayer (not a boom sprayer), and only by trained, healthy adults (not pregnant or breastfeeding women). Keep rows north–south, grow resistant varieties, conserve friendly insects, and don't grow okra (bhindi) near cotton.
Friendly insects: chrysoperla, ladybird beetles, predatory mites, spiders, dragonflies and trichogramma. Trichogramma and chrysoperla egg cards (10 to 15 per acre every 7 days, from Agriculture Department offices) control pink, spotted and American bollworms.
Jassid (green, 3 mm, two black spots on wings; leaf edges curl down and turn red; worse in humid rainy weather). Threshold 1 adult or nymph per leaf. Per acre: flonicamid 50% 60 to 80 g, or dinotefuran 20% 100 g, or sulfoxaflor 30 g, or dimethoate 40 250 to 300 ml, or acephate 75 250 to 300 g, or chlorfenapyr 360 100 ml.
Whitefly (sucks sap, causes sooty mould and spreads leaf curl virus; worse in dry weather with weeds). Keep fields weed-free, don't grow alternate hosts (okra, brinjal, potato, tomato, cucurbits) nearby, put 8 to 10 (up to 20) yellow sticky cards per acre. Threshold 5 adults or nymphs per leaf. Per acre: pyriproxyfen 10.8 500 ml, or spirotetramat 240 250 ml (with 125 ml of adjuvant), or diafenthiuron 500 200 ml, or acetamiprid 20 125 g, or flonicamid 50 80 g, or matrine 0.5% 500 ml. Spray before sunrise or within an hour after, and increase the water volume.
Thrips (threshold 8 to 10 per leaf; silvery streaks, leaves cup upward; hot dry weather): use a recommended spray as advised by Pest Warning staff.
Aphid (sust tela; sooty mould spoils lint; worst September–October): avoid spraying if friendly insects are present; 20 chrysoperla cards per acre. Per acre: imidacloprid 200 250 ml, or thiamethoxam 25 24 g, or diafenthiuron 500 200 ml, or matrine 0.5% 500 ml.
Mites (seen with a magnifier; webbing under leaves; leaves turn reddish-yellow and drop; hot dry weather): spray water early on, keep weeds down, never let the crop go dry, spray only affected patches. Per acre: spiromesifen 240 100 ml, or fenpyroximate 200 ml, or hexythiazox 10 125 g, or diafenthiuron 500 200 ml, or chlorfenapyr 360 100 ml.
Mealybug (white powdery females; sooty mould; branches dry): keep fields and bunds weed-free, check last year's fields with a magnifier, spray only affected patches first. Per 100 litres of water: profenofos 50 800 ml, or methidathion 40 300 ml, or malathion 57% 500 ml, or imidacloprid 200 250 ml.
Termites (dry sandy soil; eat roots): use only well-rotted manure; hoe. Flood per acre chlorpyrifos 1.5 to 2 litres or fipronil 5% 1 to 1.5 litres with irrigation.
Grasshopper (tokka; cuts young plants): keep fields and bunds clean of grass. Per acre: acephate 75 250 to 300 g, or lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5% 330 ml, or bifenthrin 10 250 to 330 ml.
Dusky and red cotton bugs (stain lint, bolls don't open; dusky threshold 10 per boll; September–November): plough after the last picking, pick bugs by hand early, remove alternate hosts and weeds, control in winter hiding places, encourage predators. Per acre: imidacloprid + fipronil 80 60 g, or matrine 0.5% 500 ml, or fipronil 80 30 g (red bug).
Spotted bollworm (threshold 3 larvae per 25 plants or 10 percent damage; bores shoots, squares and bolls): no okra nearby, cut and bury attacked shoots, bury fallen squares 15 July to 30 August, pheromone and light traps. Per acre: emamectin benzoate 1.9 200 ml, or lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 330 ml, or bifenthrin 10 250 ml, or chlorantraniliprole 200 50 ml, or spinetoram 120 80 ml.
Pink bollworm (threshold 5 larvae per 100 green bolls, or 10 percent damage in August / 5 percent in September; hides inside bolls, worse after rain): graze leftover bolls, use pheromone traps (4 per 20-acre block; 8 traps or PB-rope per acre on big farms, changing capsules every 15 days), stack sticks upside-down, no irrigation after 30 September and no late nitrogen, plough deep, clean ginning waste by early January, fumigate stored seed. Sprays per acre: gamma-cyhalothrin 60 100 ml, or spinetoram 120 80 ml, or triazophos 40 1,000 ml.
American bollworm (threshold 5 eggs or 3 small larvae per 25 plants; head inside the boll): check twice a week, 20 trichogramma cards per acre, traps, avoid excess fertilizer and water, irrigate and plough after picking. Spray only on eggs and young larvae, rotating: emamectin benzoate 1.9 200 ml, or spinetoram 120 60 ml, or flubendiamide 480 50 ml, or chlorantraniliprole 200 50 ml, or indoxacarb 150 175 ml, or profenofos 500 500 ml per acre.
Armyworm (feeds in groups and skeletonises plants, July–October; treat as soon as seen): spray only patches, trench with water and kerosene around fields, sow millet nearby to attract birds, light traps. Per acre: flubendiamide 480 50 ml, or lufenuron 5% 200 ml, or emamectin benzoate 1.9 200 ml, or chlorantraniliprole 50 ml, or methoxyfenozide 200 ml, or chlorfenapyr 360 100 ml, or indoxacarb 150 175 ml.
Diseases:
Cotton leaf curl virus (CLCuV): veins thicken, leaves curl inward, a small leaf-like growth forms under the leaf, plants stunt. Spread by whitefly; alternate hosts include tobacco, brinjal, okra, lantana, ber and several weeds, so control whitefly and weeds.
Bacterial blight: angular spots under young leaves turning brown-black; spreads fast in humid or rainy weather at 30 to 40 °C; bolls rot.
Twig and stem blight (fungus): black spots from twigs to branches, which wilt; severe at 30 to 35 °C and humidity above 80 percent.
Boll rot: bolls brown or black inside, don't open; bacteria spread by bugs puncturing bolls, so control all bugs.
Sooty mould (leaf blackening): from honeydew of whitefly and mites; wider plant spacing, control sucking pests, spray trifloxystrobin + tebuconazole 65 g or sulphur 250 g per 100 litres of water.
Wilt (Fusarium in hot weather, Verticillium in cooler weather; brown or black streaks inside the stem): burn affected plants, add 4 tonnes of rotted manure per acre, leave the land fallow 2 years or rotate with sorghum, maize, jantar or guar; spray a recommended fungicide (tebuconazole mixture 2 ml per litre) or flood 1 litre per acre.
Root rot (plant wilts suddenly and pulls out easily; yellow smelly roots; July–September at 7 to 8 weeks): burn affected plants, grow sorghum, maize or jantar instead of cotton for 2 to 3 years, treat seed with a fungicide.
Glyphosate on triple-gene (herbicide-tolerant) varieties: can be sprayed without a shield until 60 to 70 days, then only with a shield; keep it off tops, flowers and squares, and remove any affected plants at thinning.
aspects.sowing:
Sowing time: early sowing mid February to 31 March (best for Multan, Sahiwal, Faisalabad, Sargodha and Dera Ghazi Khan divisions); normal sowing 1 April to 31 May, best finished by 15 May (in virus-hit areas by 15 May). Late sowing yields less. To escape heat stroke (loo), finish before mid May and sow after a double pre-sowing irrigation (rauni). After wheat, temperatures above 47 °C now hurt drill-sown cotton on light and sandy soils, so sow on beds (ridges). Early sowing faces fewer sucking pests and heat effects and has more time to grow, so yield and quality are better.
Land: deep plough (or cross chisel twice) if there is a hard layer; level with a laser leveller; mix old crop residues in with a rotavator, disc harrow or soil-turning plough instead of burning.
Spacing: early crop rows 2.5 feet, plants 1.5 to 2 feet. Normal crop rows 2.5 feet: sown 1 to 30 April, plants 12 inches apart (about 17,500 per acre); sown 1 to 31 May, 9 inches (about 23,000). Best yields come at 12 to 15 inches (14,000 to 17,500 plants); at 9 inches plants compete and lower fruit drops. Adjust for soil fertility and variety. In heat and low rain, widen spacing.
Drill sowing: kharif drill, rows 2.5 feet, seed 2 to 2.5 inches deep. When plants are 1.5 to 2 feet tall, earth up every other row to form beds (saves water, eases weed control, better fertilizer use, fewer bolls drop, less lodging, safer in heavy rain).
Bed (ridge) sowing: by machine on dry beds, then irrigate keeping water 2 inches below the seed. By hand: run water 6 to 7 inches deep in the furrows, then dibble seed 1 inch above the water line; fill gaps at the next irrigation's moisture. Beds give good germination and full stand, save water and seed, protect from rain, allow spraying after rain or irrigation, and germinate better on saline land. On saline, waterlogged (barra) or low land sow on beds or ridges; make small ponds to drain extra rain.
Gap filling: sow 4 to 5 seeds soaked 5 to 6 hours per gap and cover with moist soil, quickly (late gap filling lowers yield); nursery plants can also be used.
Thinning: once, within 20 to 25 days of sowing, before the first irrigation or after dry hoeing; remove weak and diseased plants. In heavy virus areas thin after the first irrigation and remove infected plants.
Seed rate (delinted, germination 75 percent or more): early sowing 4 to 5 kg per acre (4 to 5 seeds per spot when dibbling); normal sowing delinted 6 kg, fuzzy 8 kg per acre. For drill sowing add 2 to 3 kg; keep 10 percent extra for gaps; at 60 percent germination raise to 5 to 6 kg (early) or 8 to 10 kg.
Germination test: soak 100 seeds 7 to 8 hours, spread on a wet towel, cover and keep moist; count sprouted seeds after 4 to 5 days.
Delinting: in a plastic tub pour commercial sulphuric acid slowly over the seed (1 to 1.5 litres per 10 kg seed) and stir with a wooden paddle until the seed turns shiny black, then wash in a sieve under running water; dry in the sun and store in jute or cloth bags. Machines are also available. Keep people under 18 away from acid and seed treatment, and wear gloves, closed shoes and full clothes.
Seed treatment (protects about a month from sucking pests, especially whitefly which spreads leaf curl virus): per kg of seed, imidacloprid + tebuconazole 372.5 at 10 ml, or azoxystrobin + clothianidin 62.5% at 9 g, or azoxystrobin + clothianidin + fludioxonil 72% WS at 9 g; also a fungicide.
aspects.varieties:
Grow any variety approved by the Punjab Seed Council that suits your area; buy certified, pure, healthy seed from the Punjab Seed Corporation or registered companies.
Early sowing: only triple-gene varieties are recommended (resistant to glyphosate weedkiller and to bollworms, especially pink bollworm, but not armyworm). Make sure seed is certified by the Federal Seed Certification and Registration Department and is pure triple-gene, or glyphosate will kill non-triple-gene plants.
Bt varieties (resist bollworms) and their areas:
All cotton areas of Punjab: CKC-1, CEMB-100, NIAB Sitara-M, NIAB-898, IR NIBGE-13, IR NIBGE-15, IR NIBGE-16, Weal-AG-9 (also good for low-water areas), Weal-AG-1606.
South Punjab (Multan, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Vehari, Khanewal, DG Khan, Rahim Yar Khan, Bahawalnagar, Rajanpur, Muzaffargarh, Layyah, often also Faisalabad and Sahiwal): CKC-3, Hataf-3, ICI-2424, NIAB-1011, MNH-1016, MNH-1020, MNH-1026, MNH-1050, BS-20, RH-668, CIM-663, Cyto-535; Saim-32 and Saim-102 (Multan, Bahawalpur, DG Khan, Sahiwal divisions); IUB-13, IUB-222, BS-15, BS-52 (south plus Sahiwal, Okara, Pakpattan); CIM-678 and CIM-785 (south plus Jhang and Mianwali; CIM-785 also Faisalabad, Kasur, Okara, Toba Tek Singh).
Central Punjab (Faisalabad, Toba Tek Singh, Sahiwal, Okara, Pakpattan, Jhang and others): NIAB-1048, NIAB-545, FH-Super; wide areas from Faisalabad to the south: NIAB-878B, FH-490, FH-492, FH-Anmol, IR NIBGE-2, Eagle-2. IR NIBGE-3701 suits Haroonabad, Chishtian, Bahawalpur and Rahim Yar Khan.
Non-Bt varieties: NIAB Kiran, NIAB-2008, NIAB-112, MNH-786, GS Ali-7, Cyto-226 (virus tolerant), NIBGE-2, NN-3. Keep about 10 percent of the cotton area under non-Bt varieties so bollworms don't become resistant to Bt; spray those only at the threshold.
In heat and low rain choose short-duration, heat-tolerant varieties (Ayub Agricultural Research Institute has developed several).
Heat protection: heat-tolerant varieties, early sowing where land is free, evening or night irrigation, light frequent irrigation, enough potash and micronutrients (boron, zinc, sulphur), and biostimulants or amino acids if fruit is shedding.
Leaf curl virus protection: resistant varieties; destroy weeds and cotton stubble by 31 January; control whitefly chemically and biologically (spray before or just after sunrise, rotate products) and on spring crops; if attack is early, thin later and remove infected plants; spray zinc sulphate 33% 250 g + borax 250 g + magnesium sulphate 300 g in 100 litres of water at 60, 75 and 90 days.
Bacterial blight: resistant varieties; after acid delinting soak seed 2 hours in streptomycin sulphate 1 g per litre (or hot water 50 to 55 °C for 10 to 15 minutes); at first signs spray copper oxychloride or oxathiapiprolin as advised (250 to 300 ml per acre); don't over-water or over-fertilize.
Twig and stem blight: treat delinted seed with a fungicide; spray azoxystrobin + difenoconazole 200 ml or difenoconazole 250 125 ml per acre.
Thrips: careful irrigation of young plants, weed-free fields, seed treatment; on beds, break the beds 1 to 1.5 months after sowing and make furrows between. At threshold per acre: spinetoram 120 60 ml, or chlorfenapyr 360 75 ml, or acephate 75 250 to 300 g, or flonicamid 50 60 to 80 g, or dinotefuran 20 100 g.
aspects.weeds:
Main weeds: itsit, madhana grass, wild amaranth, lehli, tandla, hazardani, khabbal and della; newer ones include makra, lehal, gajar booti (parthenium), chhirra and bhabula. Weeds cut yield, shelter pests, compete for food, water, air and light, hinder field work, spread leaf curl virus and mealybug, and release harmful chemicals. Pests often start on weeds along watercourses, bunds and roadsides, so clean these before sowing; also destroy host plants and leftover spring vegetables.
Pre-emergence (within 24 hours of sowing; on beds spray within 24 hours and never mix it into the soil): per acre pendimethalin 33 EC 1,000 to 1,250 ml, or S-metolachlor 960 EC 800 ml, or metolachlor 960 EC 800 ml, or S-metolachlor + pendimethalin 960 EC 900 ml, or acetochlor + pendimethalin 42 EC 1,000 ml. Use carefully on sandy soil. Best method: spray level land, then plank and sow (or spray then irrigate; or after rauni plank at wattar, spray, then sow).
Post-emergence (with a shield and jet nozzle; not if rain is expected): mixed weeds – glyphosate 1,500 to 1,800 ml per 100 litres of water with a shield; swanki grass – haloxyfop 10.8 or quizalofop 10.8 at 400 ml per 100 litres.
Triple-gene varieties: spray glyphosate when all weeds have emerged, about 25 to 30 days after crop emergence, preferably before thinning (so non-resistant plants die first); effects show in 8 to 10 days and weeds die within about a month. Spray in moist soil; if the crop is short of water first give 2 kg urea per acre. Don't exceed the dose. Without a shield only until 60 to 70 days.
Hoeing: dry hoeing before the first irrigation, 2 to 2.5 inches deep, without throwing soil onto plants in the rows; then hoe after every irrigation or rain at wattar until plants are too big. Tractor, ridger, rotary hoe (very useful on beds early) or labour can be used. Use integrated weed control so weeds don't become resistant.
Sprayer care: calibrate, keep speed and pressure even, good nozzles, spray in the morning or evening, not in strong wind, use clean water (not canal water), bury empty bottles. Never hoe right after a weedicide spray, and irrigate after a suitable gap.

timing.sowing: 15 February to 31 March (early) and 1 April to 31 May (normal; best by 15 May)
timing.harvesting: picking September to November (start at 40 to 50 percent open bolls)
